question: A combination of two lenses of power +2.0 D and -0.25 D is equivalent to a single lens of power:
solution:
The correct answer is __**+1.75 D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **power** of a lens is measured in **diopters (D)**.
 
• The power of a combination of lenses is equal to the **algebraic sum** of the powers of the individual lenses.
 
• Given lens powers: **+2.0 D** and **-0.25 D**.
 
• To find the equivalent power, add the powers of the two lenses:
 
• **+2.0 D + (-0.25 D) = +1.75 D**.
 
• Thus, the combination of these two lenses is equivalent to a single lens of power **+1.75 D**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lens Power**__

 __
 
• **Diopter (D)** is the unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens.
 
• A lens with a power of **+1 diopter** brings parallel rays of light to focus at **1 meter**.
 
• The power of a lens is the **reciprocal** of its focal length in meters (P = 1/f).
 
• Positive power indicates a **converging lens**, while negative power indicates a **diverging lens**.
 
 
 
• **Combination of Lenses**__
 
 
• When lenses are combined, their **individual powers** add algebraically.
 
• This is useful in **optical instruments** like microscopes and telescopes.
 
• It is important to consider the sign of the power for accurate calculations.
